failure_summary.description: Repeated base flight or restaurant searches instead of retrieving compatible cached results and applying newly added filters.
Confused hotel stars with guest ratings, altered a neighborhood name, or treated a named attraction as a category.
Treated acceptance of an offered new attraction category as a proximity request using already-cached results.
Called a hotel search without mandatory check-in and check-out dates instead of requesting the missing details.
Repeated searches for cached flight legs after a traveler-count update, although flight tools do not support passenger count.

patch.reasoning: The most frequent failure is restarting a search when a compatible cached candidate set can be filtered. A clearer boundary for common refinement cases addresses those repeats. The field-mapping clarification resolves the observed ambiguity around hotel star classifications and named attractions. The other failures are already directly covered by the required-argument, offer-resolution, and no-op rules, so duplicating those rules is unwarranted.

edits.content: **Filter covered results rather than restarting:** If a cached result's domain, location or route, dates, and candidate scope cover the request, a newly added supported filter is still a filter-only update. For example, add a neighborhood filter to a compatible city-wide restaurant result, or airline/class filters to a compatible flight-leg result: retrieve the exact cache key, call the matching `filter_*` tool with the new constraints, and save its result. Repeat a base search only when the requested candidate scope is not covered by the cache.

edits.target: For restaurant ratings and hotel guest ratings, interpret a requested “N-star rating” or “N or higher” as a minimum threshold unless the user explicitly requests an exact rating; use the inclusive range `[N, 5]` in `rating`. Use `[N, N]` only for an explicitly exact rating.
edits.content: Disambiguate the field before setting rating bounds. A hotel described by its N-star classification—including “a 1-star rating” when guest-review context is absent—uses `stars`, not `rating`; an exact N-star classification uses `[N, N]`, while “at least N stars” uses `[N, 5]`. Use `rating` for hotel guest/review scores and restaurant ratings; treat “N or higher” as `[N, 5]` unless an exact score is explicitly requested, in which case use `[N, N]`. For attractions, pass a named place in `attraction_name` exactly as given; use `type` only for an explicitly requested category, and do not infer a category from words in a proper name. Preserve the complete user-provided neighborhood phrase in `neighborhood`, including any city qualifier, and pass the surrounding city separately in `city`.
